answer_text:
Let \(K=\overline{\mathbb{Q}}\) be the algebraic closure of \(\mathbb{Q}\), viewed as the field of algebraic numbers inside \(\mathbb{C}\). A \(\mathbb{Q}\)-field homomorphism
\[
\sigma:K\to \mathbb{C}
\]
satisfies \(\sigma(q)=q\) for every \(q\in\mathbb{Q}\).

First, \(\sigma\) is injective, since a unital field homomorphism has no nonzero kernel. Let \(F=\sigma(K)\). If \(\alpha\in K\), then \(\alpha\) is algebraic over \(\mathbb{Q}\), so \(\sigma(\alpha)\) satisfies the same minimal polynomial over \(\mathbb{Q}\). Hence \(\sigma(\alpha)\in \overline{\mathbb{Q}}=K\), so \(F\subseteq K\).

Also, \(F\) is algebraically closed because it is isomorphic to \(K\). If \(\beta\in K\), then \(\beta\) is algebraic over \(\mathbb{Q}\subseteq F\). Since \(F\) is algebraically closed, \(\beta\in F\). Therefore \(F=K\). Thus every such \(\sigma\) is actually a \(\mathbb{Q}\)-automorphism of \(K\), i.e. an element of \(\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q})\).

Now count these automorphisms.

**Upper bound.** Since \(K\) is countable, the set of all functions \(K\to\mathbb{C}\) has cardinality at most
\[
|\mathbb{C}|^{\aleph_0}=(2^{\aleph_0})^{\aleph_0}=2^{\aleph_0}.
\]
So there are at most \(2^{\aleph_0}\) such homomorphisms.

**Lower bound.** Let \(p_1,p_2,\dots\) be the primes. For each choice of signs
\[
\varepsilon=(\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2,\dots)\in\{\pm1\}^{\mathbb{N}},
\]
define on
\[
L=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{p_1},\sqrt{p_2},\dots)
\]
the map
\[
\sqrt{p_n}\longmapsto \varepsilon_n\sqrt{p_n}.
\]
For every finite set of primes, this gives an automorphism of
\[
\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{p_1},\dots,\sqrt{p_m}),
\]
and these finite automorphisms are compatible, so they define an automorphism of \(L\). By the extension theorem for algebraic closures, this automorphism extends to a \(\mathbb{Q}\)-automorphism of \(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}\).

Different sign sequences give different automorphisms, because they send some \(\sqrt{p_n}\) to different values. There are \(2^{\aleph_0}\) sign sequences, so there are at least \(2^{\aleph_0}\) homomorphisms.

Combining the upper and lower bounds, the number of such \(\mathbb{Q}\)-field homomorphisms is exactly

\[
\boxed{2^{\aleph_0}}
\]
